name: Link
description: Navigates somewhere else, inline or in chrome, with real link semantics.

tone.description: Colour. accent is the link ink; neutral reads in ink 1 and keeps it on hover

external.description: Opens in new tab with noopener noreferrer

render.description: Replaces the rendered element (a router link); the look and props move onto it

when: Pointing out to docs or external resources
whenNot: A main call to action — use Button
Switching views in place — use Tabs
guidelines: external sets target and rel; add your own "opens in a new tab" cue
Always underlined: one hairline at the shared offset, so a link never relies on colour alone
tone="neutral" for quiet links in dense copy and footers
accessibility: The link text alone should make sense out of context
Say when a link opens a new window
A link that looks like a button still needs link semantics

examples.name: Tones
examples.description: The link ink, then the neutral ink.
examples.code:
import { Stack } from '@/components/Stack';

<Stack direction="row" gap="md" align="center" wrap>
  <Link href="#" tone="accent">Accent</Link>
  <Link href="#" tone="neutral">Neutral</Link>
</Stack>

examples.name: External Link
examples.description: Sets target and rel; you still supply the visible cue.

examples.name: Render
examples.description: Moves the look onto a router link.
examples.code:
import RouterLink from "next/link";

<Link render={<RouterLink href="/pricing" />}>Client-side navigation</Link>

relations.note: Use Button for primary actions, Link for navigation
Links often appear within Text components

propsSummary: external: boolean - opens in new tab
render: element | function - replaces the rendered element (router links)
